speakers.name: Pat McFadden
speakers.role: The Secretary of State for Work and Pensions

contributions.text: 2. What recent progress he has made on implementing the youth guarantee.
contributions.name: Andrew Lewin

contributions.who: The Secretary of State for Work and Pensions (Pat McFadden)
contributions.text: We are delivering the youth guarantee to support young people across Great Britain. We have introduced more intensive, earlier support in jobcentres, expanded the network of youth hubs—more than 175 are now open—and introduced a youth jobs grant and the jobs guarantee nationally. I announced last week that, from next April, we will bring forward eligibility for the jobs guarantee so that it is available for young people who have been on universal credit for 12 months rather than 18 months.
contributions.name: Pat McFadden
contributions.role: The Secretary of State for Work and Pensions

contributions.text: I thank the Secretary of State for all that we are doing to champion opportunities for young people. When I last met with my jobcentre in Hatfield, representatives said that employers on the youth guarantee scheme had a mixed record. Some firms were embracing the scheme, and were great partners to work with, but others were more reluctant. Will the Secretary of State tell me a bit more about what work is being done to encourage and incentivise as many businesses as possible to embrace the youth guarantee?
contributions.name: Andrew Lewin

contributions.text: I commend my hon. Friend for working with his jobcentre and local employers. The truth is that we need to ensure that offers such as this are as simple as possible for employers to use. It is a challenge to ensure that the information is as user friendly and as simple to access as possible, especially for small and medium-sized businesses that do not have big human resources departments and so on. However, employers are signing up: earlier this month the waste management company Biffa announced that it would be offering up to 2,000 jobs to young people through the youth guarantee. I welcomed that announcement on a recent visit to one of its sites.
contributions.name: Pat McFadden
contributions.role: The Secretary of State for Work and Pensions

contributions.text: Has the Secretary of State’s Department undertaken a labour market assessment of the Government’s new proposals for the EU mobility scheme, and what those will mean for the implementation of the youth guarantee scheme and the aim of getting more British young people back into work?
contributions.name: Priti Patel

contributions.text: I do not share what I think is the implication behind the right hon. Lady’s question—that there is direct competition in this way. I think a closer relationship with the European Union is in our economic interests. It is in the interests of economic growth and business dynamism, and economic growth and business dynamism are what create jobs in the first place.
contributions.name: Pat McFadden
contributions.role: The Secretary of State for Work and Pensions
